items.title: T-DIG: Text-Conditioned Diversity for Image Generation
items.summary: T-DIG is a text-conditioned diversity framework that uses an LLM policy with reinforcement learning to generate axis-specific image variations via frozen generators, enabling user-directed exploration without model retraining.

items.title: Multiscale Policy Optimization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
items.summary: Multiscale Policy Optimization improves long-horizon agent training by aligning credit assignment and policy updates at the turn scale.

items.title: h1: A Taste of the Bitter Lesson in Automated Theorem Proving
items.summary: A simple agentic loop with efficient Lean feedback achieves state-of-the-art formal theorem proving without structured workflows, showing that execution interfaces matter more than complex orchestration.

items.title: The Lexical Imprint of Pre-training Data
items.summary: Pre-training corpora leave a lexical imprint on zero-shot accuracy that is consistently tracked by word-level unigram cross-entropy across benchmarks, document selection, and prompt routing.

items.title: Zooming without Zooming v2: From Seeing Details to Connecting Evidence for Generalizable Multimodal Perception
items.summary: EvidenceConnect synthesizes training data to strengthen visual evidence connection, improving spatial perception and multimodal reasoning across diverse tasks.

items.title: Can Discrete Tokens Serve as Semantically Lossless Representations of Visual Signals?
items.summary: Factorized Vector Quantization improves discrete visual token quality by using parallel codebooks on complementary feature views, enabling discrete representations to match continuous ones in multimodal understanding.

items.title: Truncate or Not? A Scaling Study of Looped Transformers with Truncated Backpropagation
items.summary: Looped transformers trained with full backpropagation through time outperform truncated alternatives under matched compute, with scaling laws identifying two loops as optimal when model size is adjustable.

items.title: Rare, Relevant, and Still Wrong: How Memory Fails LLM Group Decisions
items.summary: When compressing multi-agent discussions for final decisions, memory selection by rarity or relevance both fail due to decoy inclusion and social-proof bias, and even full transcripts reduce accuracy compared to no notes.

items.title: VibeVideoBench: Evaluating Multimodal Agents on Code-Driven Video Generation
items.summary: VibeVideoBench evaluates multimodal agents that generate videos via code, finding that top systems meet core requirements on most tasks but frequently fail due to poor time management.

items.title: RynnWorld-Latent: A Cross-Embodiment World Model Conditioned on Universal Latent Actions
items.summary: RynnWorld-Latent learns cross-embodiment world dynamics via 3D-grounded latent actions, enabling joint pretraining on diverse video sources and synthetic data generation for improved robot policy performance.

items.title: PDRVLA: A Vision-Language-Action Model with Physical Dynamics Representations
items.summary: PDRVLA improves robot action generation by integrating a lightweight physical dynamics module that predicts future visual features with world-model supervision, avoiding online video generation latency.

items.title: Your Policy Is Secretly a Harness: The Decision Geometry of Agent Interfaces
items.summary: Under KL-regularized control, a policy encodes its harness preferences, so deployed performance equals harness potential minus policy mismatch, and harness comparisons must separate these terms to predict training gains.

items.title: Benchmarking Obstacle-Conditioned Safety in Household Robot Navigation
items.summary: The study introduces a benchmark and metric to evaluate whether robot navigation policies adapt continuous motion to obstacle safety semantics, revealing a gap in translating semantic caution into safe movement.

items.title: The Trinity:Capability-Driven Recursive Self-Improvement for Multimodal Agents
items.summary: The Trinity framework recursively improves multimodal agents by organizing tasks into a capability tree, generating simulated training worlds, and routing specialized harness modules to boost performance on diverse benchmarks.

items.title: PhysEvolve: Verifier-grounded Self-evolution for Physical Reasoning with Executable Worlds
items.summary: Physevolve trains vision-language models in causal physical reasoning by using a physics engine to validate self-generated executable worlds and counterfactual simulations, improving performance on dynamics benchmarks without human data.

items.title: MoveBench: A Rubric-Based Benchmark for Evaluating Large Language Models in Sports and Health Coaching
items.summary: MoveBench introduces a specialized benchmark for evaluating large language models on sports and health coaching, emphasizing safety, scientific validity, and personalization across multiple-choice and open-ended tasks.

items.title: MLE-World: Predicting Machine Learning Experiment Outcomes with a Learned World Model
items.summary: A world model predicts machine learning program outcomes to enable affordable test-time scaling for AI research agents, improving performance with fewer real executions.

items.title: Vision-Language-Action or World-Action? Just Action Models
items.summary: Just Action Model decouples backbone initialization, future observation objectives, and inference machinery to improve robot control with foresight training and reduced computation.

items.title: Timestral
items.summary: Timestral is a family of time series foundation models that achieves state-of-the-art probabilistic forecasting through decoupled horizon forecasting, native future covariate support, and synthetic pretraining followed by mixed post-training.

items.title: Learning and Reasoning with Geometry: How Generation Helps Spatial Understanding
items.summary: GeoUG improves spatial reasoning by combining depth and multi-view generation with adaptive geometric verification during inference.

items.title: Channel Selection for Mixture-of-Experts Decoding Needs No Calibration Data
items.summary: Prox replaces calibrated thresholds with top-k channel selection and a weight-derived reader to accelerate Mixture-of-Experts inference while preserving accuracy.

items.title: OvisOCR3 Technical Report
items.summary: OvisOCR3 is a compact 0.8B vision-language model that unifies diverse OCR tasks through multi-teacher distillation and reinforcement learning, achieving state-of-the-art results across document parsing, general OCR, key information extraction, figure captioning, and cross-page table reconstruction.

items.title: CodeCap-Bench: Can Code Serve as a Good Video Caption?
items.summary: Executable code representations of video content improve reasoning and reconstruction over natural language, yet current multimodal models still struggle to generate faithful code captions for complex temporal dynamics.

items.title: Memory Tax: Dissecting the Net Value of Agent Memory
items.summary: Large-scale evaluation reveals that dedicated memory systems often underperform naive retrieval-augmented generation, introducing a framework of memory benefit and memory tax to assess net value.

items.title: ThinkWorld: World Imagination Reinforces Chain-of-Dynamics Reasoning
items.summary: ThinkWorld improves robotic generalization by representing actions as dynamics chains and using world imagination to learn from unlabeled human videos.

items.title: MatAnyone-E: Sparse Memory Propagation for Efficient High-Resolution Video Matting
items.summary: MatAnyone-E accelerates high-resolution video matting by selectively applying high-resolution matching to uncertain regions and using a lightweight decoder, achieving large speedups with preserved quality.

items.title: Omni-InteractScope: Benchmarking Proactive and Agentic Interaction in Continuous Omnimodal Streams
items.summary: Omni-InteractScope evaluates continuous audiovisual interaction reliability, revealing that current Omni-LLMs struggle with timely tool use, query-free reminders, and sustained guidance.

items.title: HABIT-Bench: Evaluating Habit Induction from Longitudinal Weak Evidence in Agent Memory
items.summary: HABIT-Bench evaluates whether LLM agent memory systems can infer implicit user habits from sparse dialogue evidence and apply them correctly across long-term interactions.

items.title: Can Test-Time Memory Evolution Outperform Test-Time Training for Scientific Discovery?
items.summary: Test-Time Memory Evolution updates external memory without changing model weights to guide scientific discovery more efficiently than test-time training.

items.title: SearchHorizonBench: A Benchmark for Search Value in AI Agents
items.summary: SearchHorizonBench evaluates how agents learn to estimate the value of additional search from execution history, showing that historical calibration improves prediction accuracy but leaves most search-gain variance unexplained.

items.title: Hy-Nomas: Towards Free-form Interactive World Generation
items.summary: Hy-Nomas is a video world model that uses causal attention and structured captions to follow multi-turn text and camera instructions while preserving interaction history.

items.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
items.summary: LongChang evaluates whether LLMs can autonomously discover altered physical laws through simulated experimentation, finding that only one model achieved limited success.

items.title: Harness-Model Collaboration for Long-Horizon Continual Learning
items.summary: HaMo combines rapid retrieval of procedural experience cards with gradual model adaptation to improve long-horizon web agents' retention and cross-task execution.

items.title: What Effort Level Should I Choose? On the Economics of Reasoning Effort in LLM Agents
items.summary: Reasoning effort in generative models acts as a credence good where higher compute does not guarantee better instance-level results, and an escalation strategy from low effort improves cost-efficiency.

items.title: Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion-Uni: Elastic Self-Refining Unified Diffusion LLM with Cross-Paradigm On-Policy Distillation
items.summary: NLD-Uni is a unified discrete diffusion language model that combines visual understanding and generation via cross-paradigm on-policy distillation and progressive self-refining diffusion.

items.title: RSI Arena: Towards Recursive Self-Improvement with Human Feedback
items.summary: RSI Arena demonstrates that autonomous AI agents can independently train and iteratively improve language models using human feedback, with most agents achieving preference gains in a second stage despite modest benchmark improvements.

items.title: ChronoReplay: One Answer Interface Is Not Enough for Streaming Spatial Intelligence
items.summary: ChronoReplay mitigates interface lock-in in spatial vision-language models by replaying heterogeneous spatial supervision chronologically, improving cross-task transfer and enabling efficient inference-time evidence selection.

items.title: Cross-modal Steering Vectors Exist Across Both Image and Text Generation
items.summary: Cross-modal steering vectors transfer between text and image generation in unified multimodal models, revealing shared causal control mechanisms despite a modality gap.

items.title: LociArt: A Unified Paradigm for Free-Style Local Video Stylization
items.summary: LociArt enables precise local video stylization with region-style control and temporal consistency via a generative refinement network, automated dataset construction, and a dedicated benchmark.

items.title: On the SPOT: Enhancing Speculative Decoding for Diffusion Language Models via Commit-Order Prediction
items.summary: SPOT accelerates diffusion language models by predicting token generation order and verifying candidates in parallel, reducing passes up to 6.8x while maintaining exact decoding.

items.title: Rollback: Experience Backtracking in World Models for Policy Improvement
items.summary: Rollback improves robot policies by using world models to rewind to past decisions, explore counterfactual actions, and generate fine-grained supervision, while continuously refining dynamics via real-world feedback.

items.title: OpenESM: Energy-Steered Models Are Scalable Foundation Learners
items.summary: Energy-steered models integrate energy-guided latent optimization with token generation to improve foundational language modeling and scale effectively across diverse tasks.

items.title: CellTrack-Bench: Microscopic Cell Tracking Benchmark for Vision-Language Models
items.summary: A new benchmark evaluates vision-language models on cell tracking against specialized algorithms, revealing reasoning gaps across diverse imaging modalities.

items.title: SO-101 Bench: Accessible Spatial Manipulation
items.summary: A simulated benchmark for language-conditioned spatial manipulation on low-cost robot arms reveals that hybrid LLM agents outperform learned vision-language-action policies, with ranking consistency between simulation and real hardware.

items.title: Ψ-0.6: Adaptive Streams of Thought in a Unified Vision-Language World Model
items.summary: A unified vision-language world model adaptively combines perception, language, geometry, and simulation through interleaved reasoning streams to improve spatial reasoning and counterfactual simulation.

items.title: ParetoRSI-Gym: Can AI Agents Improve Language Models Across Multiple Domains?
items.summary: ParetoRSI-Gym evaluates recursive self-improvement agents across multiple domains by fixing the model and pipeline while allowing data curation and training loops, revealing significant generalization gains and distinct agent strategies.

items.title: How Far Can Coding Agents Go in Visual Generation?
items.summary: Coding agents build images via executable programs, showing structured visual reasoning and consistent internal scene representations across drawing interfaces.

items.title: Representation Redistribution in Sparse Autoencoders
items.summary: Sparse autoencoders decompose language model activations into sparse features, and the redistribution sensitivity score identifies recurring feature changes that contribute to downstream readout failures without equating representation change with failure.

items.title: EnvLunch: The Environment as a Free Lunch for Learning to Interact
items.summary: EnvLunch leverages executable environments to generate verifiable training trajectories without human annotations, improving agent performance and reducing labeled data requirements for downstream tasks.

items.title: Did the Model Use That? Counterfactual Training Boosts Self-Attribution in Language Models
items.summary: CREDIT improves language model self-attribution of external information via counterfactual training, reducing false acknowledgment of non-influential sources.
